NASB.1: Then Job answered the LORD and said,
NASB.2: 'I know that You can do all things, And that no purpose of Yours can be thwarted.
NASB.3: 'Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge?' 'Therefore I have declared that which I did not understand, Things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.'
NASB.4: 'Hear, now, and I will speak; I will ask You, and You instruct me.'
NASB.5: 'I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear; But now my eye sees You;
NASB.6: Therefore I retract, And I repent in dust and ashes.'
NASB.7: It came about after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, that the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, 'My wrath is kindled against you and against your two friends, because you have not spoken of Me what is right as My servant Job has.
NASB.8: 'Now therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to My servant Job, and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and My servant Job will pray for you. For I will accept him so that I may not do with you [according to your] folly, because you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has.'
NASB.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite [and] Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD told them; and the LORD accepted Job.
NASB.10: The LORD restored the fortunes of Job when he prayed for his friends, and the LORD increased all that Job had twofold.
NASB.11: Then all his brothers and all his sisters and all who had known him before came to him, and they ate bread with him in his house; and they consoled him and comforted him for all the adversities that the LORD had brought on him. And each one gave him one piece of money, and each a ring of gold.
NASB.12: The LORD blessed the latter [days] of Job more than his beginning; and he had 14,000 sheep and 6,000 camels and 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys.
NASB.13: He had seven sons and three daughters.
NASB.14: He named the first Jemimah, and the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
NASB.15: In all the land no women were found so fair as Job's daughters; and their father gave them inheritance among their brothers.
NASB.16: After this, Job lived 140 years, and saw his sons and his grandsons, four generations.
NASB.17: And Job died, an old man and full of days.

ESV.1: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
ESV.2: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted.
ESV.3: ‘Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I have uttered what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
ESV.4: ‘Hear, and I will speak; I will question you, and you make it known to me.’
ESV.5: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you;
ESV.6: therefore I despise myself, and repent  in dust and ashes.”
ESV.7: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite: “My anger burns against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.
ESV.8: Now therefore take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves. And my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept his prayer not to deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.”
ESV.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.
ESV.10: And the LORD restored the fortunes of Job, when he had prayed for his friends. And the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
ESV.11: Then came to him all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before, and ate bread with him in his house. And they showed him sympathy and comforted him for all the evil  that the LORD had brought upon him. And each of them gave him a piece of money  and a ring of gold.
ESV.12: And the LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning. And he had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
ESV.13: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
ESV.14: And he called the name of the first daughter Jemimah, and the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-happuch.
ESV.15: And in all the land there were no women so beautiful as Job's daughters. And their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
ESV.16: And after this Job lived 140 years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, four generations.
ESV.17: And Job died, an old man, and full of days.

NKJV.1: Then Job answered the LORD and said:
NKJV.2: “I know that You can do everything, And that no purpose of Yours can be withheld from You.
NKJV.3: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I have uttered what I did not understand, Things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
NKJV.4: Listen, please, and let me speak; You said, ‘I will question you, and you shall answer Me.’
NKJV.5: “I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear, But now my eye sees You.
NKJV.6: Therefore I abhor myself, And repent in dust and ashes.”
NKJV.7: And so it was, after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, that the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is aroused against you and your two friends, for you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has.
NKJV.8: Now therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and My servant Job shall pray for you. NKJV.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD commanded them; for the LORD had accepted Job.
NKJV.10: And the LORD restored Job’s losses when he prayed for his friends. Indeed the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
NKJV.11: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been his acquaintances before, came to him and ate food with him in his house; and they consoled him and comforted him for all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. NKJV.12: Now the LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning; for he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female donkeys.
NKJV.13: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
NKJV.14: And he called the name of the first Jemimah, the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
NKJV.15: In all the land were found no women so beautiful as the daughters of Job; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
NKJV.16: After this Job lived one hundred and forty years, and saw his children and grandchildren for four generations.
NKJV.17: So Job died, old and full of days.

NLT.1: Then Job replied to the LORD:
NLT.2:
“I know that you can do anything,
and no one can stop you.
NLT.3:
You asked, ‘Who is this that questions my wisdom with such ignorance?’
It is I — and I was talking about things I knew nothing about,
things far too wonderful for me.
NLT.4:
You said, ‘Listen and I will speak!
I have some questions for you,
and you must answer them.’
NLT.5:
I had only heard about you before,
but now I have seen you with my own eyes.
NLT.6:
I take back everything I said,
and I sit in dust and ashes to show my repentance.”
NLT.7: After the LORD had finished speaking to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite: “I am angry with you and your two friends, for you have not spoken accurately about me, as my servant Job has.
NLT.8: So take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer on your behalf. I will not treat you as you deserve, for you have not spoken accurately about me, as my servant Job has.”
NLT.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite did as the LORD commanded them, and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer.
NLT.10: When Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes. In fact, the LORD gave him twice as much as before!
NLT.11: Then all his brothers, sisters, and former friends came and feasted with him in his home. And they consoled him and comforted him because of all the trials the LORD had brought against him. And each of them brought him a gift of money and a gold ring.
NLT.12: So the LORD blessed Job in the second half of his life even more than in the beginning. For now he had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 teams of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
NLT.13: He also gave Job seven more sons and three more daughters.
NLT.14: He named his first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
NLT.15: In all the land no women were as lovely as the daughters of Job. And their father put them into his will along with their brothers.
NLT.16: Job lived 140 years after that, living to see four generations of his children and grandchildren.
NLT.17: Then he died, an old man who had lived a long, full life.

I will question you, and you declare to me.’
NRSVCE.5:
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear,
but now my eye sees you;
NRSVCE.6:
therefore I despise myself,
and repent in dust and ashes.”
NRSVCE.7: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite: “My wrath is kindled against you and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.
NRSVCE.8: Now therefore take seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept his prayer not to deal with you according to your folly; for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has done.”
NRSVCE.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer.
NRSVCE.10: And the LORD restored the fortunes of Job when he had prayed for his friends; and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
NRSVCE.11: Then there came to him all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before, and they ate bread with him in his house; they showed him sympathy and comforted him for all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him; and each of them gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.
NRSVCE.12: The LORD blessed the latter days of Job more than his beginning; and he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand donkeys.
NRSVCE.13: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
NRSVCE.14: He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
NRSVCE.15: In all the land there were no women so beautiful as Job’s daughters; and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
NRSVCE.16: After this Job lived one hundred and forty years, and saw his children, and his children’s children, four generations.
NRSVCE.17: And Job died, old and full of days.

NET.2: “I know that you can do all things; no purpose of yours can be thwarted;
NET.3: you asked, ‘Who is this who darkens counsel without knowledge?’ But I have declared without understanding things too wonderful for me to know.
NET.4: You said, ‘Pay attention, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’
NET.5: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye has seen you.
NET.6: Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes!
NET.7: After the LORD had spoken these things to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My anger is stirred up against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken about me what is right, as my servant Job has.
NET.8: So now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. And my servant Job will intercede for you, and I will respect him, so that I do not deal with you according to your folly, because you have not spoken about me what is right, as my servant Job has.”
NET.9: So they went, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and did just as the LORD had told them; and the LORD had respect for Job.
NET.10: So the LORD restored what Job had lost after he prayed for his friends, and the LORD doubled all that had belonged to Job.
NET.11: So they came to him, all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before, and they dined with him in his house. They comforted him and consoled him for all the trouble the LORD had brought on him, and each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
NET.12: So the LORD blessed the second part of Job’s life more than the first. He had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
NET.13: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.
NET.14: The first daughter he named Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-Happuch.
NET.15: Nowhere in all the land could women be found who were as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father granted them an inheritance alongside their brothers.
NET.16: After this Job lived 140 years; he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
NET.17: And so Job died, old and full of days.
